speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly how the sensation of spinning started and how long it has been lasting?

Have you noticed any associated symptoms such as hearing loss, ringing in the ears, nausea, or double vision?

Finally, did anything specific, like a recent head injury or a sudden change in position, trigger this episode?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The description of brief, spinning vertigo lasting only 3 minutes upon changing position (going to bed), without hearing loss or neurological deficits, is highly characteristic of BPPV. Given your age and history, I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the specific affected canal.
